title: Quant presets decision graph and calibration automation for model catalog
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Add an automated orchestration layer that selects a recommended quantization preset (FP8/INT8 variants + calibration parameters) for each model in the catalog, exposes a human-review decision graph in Console, and wires an automated calibration + validation run in CI before any preset is published to customers.
background: We currently maintain several hand-curated quant profiles and scattershot calibration steps. As the catalog and supported hardware grow, maintaining safe recommendations requires a reproducible workflow: a decision graph that encodes model characteristics, target latency/cost SLOs, and accuracy tolerances, plus a calibration & validation automation that runs standardized eval suites and produces confidence metrics for rollout guards.
goals: 1) Produce per-model recommended preset (primary + fallback chain) with clear guardrails. 2) Ship a Console decision-graph UI for reviewers to inspect, override, or annotate presets. 3) Integrate a CI job that runs calibration, collects eval results, and gates publishing based on pass/fail thresholds.
success_metrics:
- Fraction of catalog models with automated recommended preset >= 90%
- Number of regressions post-rollout (accuracy drift) < 1% of active models per quarter
- Manual review time per model < 20 minutes on average
acceptance_criteria: Automated decision graph produces a single recommended preset and at least one fallback for every model in staging catalog
CI calibration job completes within SLA (max 2 hours) for 95% of models in the test bed
Validation suite computes and stores confidence bands and a pass/fail signal used by rollout gating
Console exposes the decision graph and allows reviewer to add notes / force an override
Security review completed and KMS-protected artifacts for calibration outputs are stored
design_notes: Decision graph nodes include: model architecture family, layer types (presence of grouped attention), activation distribution heuristics, target hw (A100/H100/AMD), preferred quant type (FP8/INT8), calibration method (KL/MaxAbs/Per-channel), and accuracy tolerance buckets. Profiles are tagged with expected token throughput and estimated per-token cost.
technical_approach: 1) Build a ruleset that maps model metadata + lightweight probes to candidate presets. 2) Launch a containerized calibration harness that runs representative prompts and computes eval metrics (perplexity, BLEU/ROUGE on canonical tasks, and a suite of Redwood prompt tests). 3) Collect per-layer quantization sensitivity metrics and produce a confidence score. 4) Persist artifacts in the model catalog with immutable versioning. 5) Expose API + Console UX for reviewer actions.
calibration_workflow:
- Stage 1: Lightweight probe (10 sample prompts) to detect catastrophic failure modes.
- Stage 2: Full calibration (per-channel INT8 and FP8 experiments) across calibration datasets for RTT-sensitive and quality-sensitive workloads.
- Stage 3: Run validation suites (in-distribution and OOD prompt sets) and compute delta versus baseline fp32.
- Stage 4: Produce report: accuracy delta, latency/cost estimate, per-layer sensitivity, recommended fallback chains.
validation_plan: Use the canonical Redwood eval harness with three buckets: general language, instruction-following, and domain-specific sets (code, finance, healthcare). For each model/preset run: compute mean accuracy delta, 95% confidence interval via bootstrap, and per-prompt regression flags. Gate criteria: mean delta within tolerance bucket AND <2% prompts flagged as severe regressions.
rollout_plan: 1) Publish preset to staging catalog behind feature flag. 2) Canary rollout to 1% of traffic using routing policy (latency-first) for 48 hours. 3) Observe quality and telemetry (KL divergence of token distributions, customer-facing errors). 4) If no alerts, expand to 25% for 72 hours, then full release. All rollouts require one reviewer approval if automated confidence < medium.
rollback_plan: Automatic rollback triggers: accuracy gate fail, spike in user-visible error rates, or latency regressions >30% of baseline. Rollback path: switch routing to fallback model variant (FP32 or previous stable quantized variant) with automatic scaled burst capacity.
updates: 2026-02-08: Initial spike complete. Probe harness implemented and validated on 5 small models. Observed one model family with non-linear activation distributions requiring per-channel scale adjustments.
2026-02-20: Decision graph prototype created (rules + lightweight ML scorer). PM review suggested adding a human-review step for domain-sensitive models.
2026-02-28: Calibration CI runner containerized and integrated with CI. Average run time for small models ~45 minutes; large models currently ~3.4 hours (needs optimization).
2026-03-05: Security flagged need for KMS encryption for calibration artifacts; engineering added KMS hooks to pipeline (pending key rotation policy).
2026-03-11: UX review of Console decision graph - comments: surface per-layer sensitivity and allow reviewer to 'pin' fallback chain. Assigned to DES-412 for follow-up
blockers: Calibration CI resource limits for >70B models
Golden eval datasets not yet finalized for some domain buckets
decisions: Use hybrid approach: deterministic rules for initial candidate selection, followed by a learned scorer that weights calibration outcomes
Expose only recommended preset + one explicit fallback in Console to keep reviewer cognitive load low
FP8 will be labeled as 'experimental' in catalog until we can demonstrate consistent <1.5% mean accuracy delta across validation sets
risks: Overfitting calibration to small prompt sets leading to silent regressions
Long calibration times delaying shipping for large models
Insufficient telemetry to detect subtle quality issues in production
test_plan: 1) Unit tests for decision graph rule evaluation. 2) Integration test that runs calibration harness in ephemeral infra and validates artifact storage + metadata. 3) End-to-end test that publishes preset to staging and runs canary traffic simulation with synthetic prompts. 4) Fuzz tests for malformed calibration outputs.
notes: Next actions: reduce full calibration runtime via shard-based parallelism and quant sampling heuristics; finalize golden eval set with Product and Research; schedule security review meeting for 2026-03-18.
owner_expectations: Ship MVP that handles 80% of catalog models with automated presets and gating; document manual override workflow for the remaining models.
